title: What If You Never Slept Again? Day 5 Is When It Gets Strange

scenes.text: What if you never slept again? Your body would answer in a way you wouldn't expect.
In 1963, student Randy Gardner stayed awake for 264 hours, eleven full days.
By day two his eyes struggled to focus, and by day three he was moody and clumsy.
By day five he began hallucinating, and his memory and attention kept collapsing.
Rats kept from sleeping entirely died after about two to three weeks, so sleep is not optional.
Gardner slept fourteen hours afterwards, and doctors found no lasting damage. Your brain forgives. For a while.
